resolvedQuestions: The supplied aggregates identify the semicolon check as read-associated with a lower rate and the table check as not lower after reading, while leaving causation unresolved.
A card must retain the self-check for an enforcement-preserving compression hypothesis; the paired byte savings for two rules are measurable.
keyFindings: The semicolon rate is 37.0% before, 17.0% after, and 43.7% never; association is not causal.
The table rate is 17.4% before and 20.3% after; the detector also counts legitimate requested-document tables.
The five reply-time rules total 42,811 bytes, about 10.7k four-byte token-equivalents; actual per-response load and billing are unknown.
A two-rule card plus self-check pilot measures 4,757 bytes against 18,340 full bytes, a conditional 13,583-byte reduction.
Bare rule cards omit operative norms in six of thirteen files; retain self-checks in compression experiments.
The current completion Stop sentinel is asynchronous and advisory-only; it does not block or rewrite replies.
Devin AGENTS.md truncation removes the §8 pointer and is a separate runtime issue from Claude Code measurements.
ruledOutDirections: Treat observational before/after/never groups as causal estimates.
Use plain Fires when and The rule cards without self-checks as safe compression.
Treat the current completion-evidence Stop sentinel as a reply linter or rewrite hook.
Attribute the Claude Code compliance pattern to Devin AGENTS.md truncation.
Load all thirteen rule files on every response as the default cost strategy.
